source_review.notes: Checked ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 stakeholder-needs and requirements material, ISO/IEC 25010:2023 product-quality model, current SWEBOK requirements topics, and primary goal/measurement, world-machine, and value-sensitive-design sources.

evidence: Reviewed stakeholder-indexed goals, outcome-contract tuple, rate/disparity formulas, AND/OR refinement, obstacles, guardrails, and causal notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Populations, windows, units, and claim types are distinguished; descriptive formulas are not labeled causal.

evidence: Executed outcome-contract-evaluator and independently recomputed overall 0.850, subgroup rates 0.900/0.800, gap 0.100, complaint guardrail, and final failure.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Every denominator and Boolean acceptance condition in the executable example was independently checked.

evidence: Checked AND/OR refinement meaning and obstacle insufficiency.
Checked goal-question-metric direction and traceability graph.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Refinements are presented as adequacy hypotheses under assumptions rather than automatic logical entailments.

evidence: Reviewed zero/missing denominator, changed eligibility, aggregate/subgroup reversal, proxy gaming, missing non-users, small samples, stale baselines, concurrent interventions, data drift, privacy burden, and safety-critical outcomes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Outcome acceptance never bypasses guardrails, stakeholder legitimacy, data-quality review, or causal-evidence limitations.

evidence: Traced stakeholder completeness, goal refinement, outcome contract, distribution, causal evidence, and bidirectional traceability invariants through all examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: Influence is never treated as legitimacy, outputs never substitute silently for outcomes, and average success never implies subgroup success.

evidence: Reviewed formula definitions and Boolean contract composition line by line.
Reviewed adequacy and causal-claim boundaries against examples and exercises.
proof_review.notes: No general causal theorem is claimed; the code proves only evaluation of its declared aggregate rules for one dataset.

evidence: Audited all uses of prove, cause, evidence, invariant, model, effect, and adequacy language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Correlation, causal identification, measurement validity, and stakeholder legitimacy are consistently bounded and no proof sketch is disguised as a full proof.

evidence: Reviewed executable-output framing, current-standard statements, measurement examples, and safety limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The code is deterministic arithmetic evidence only. No field effectiveness, causal, clinical, railway, or external review claim is made.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed role distinctions, stakeholder exposure/authority, goals, refinements, outcomes, proxies, guardrails, conflict governance, causal evidence, and lifecycle traceability for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed discovery practices, denominator/data-quality rules, distributional monitoring, proxy gaming, experiment alternatives, privacy burden, accountable decisions, and retirement triggers. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from stakeholder mapping through goals, outcome contracts, measurement, conflicts, and causal humility; ten examples and five answered exercises provide distinct retrieval-to-transfer work.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
